solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Showing off by the actor due a TV part?

indicators.note: read as 'showing' the letters 'off' their usual order, so the words before the definition are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sneer at an actor hamming it up because a television role is coming his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing off' looks like a description of the actor's vanity, but it is the anagram signal; all fourteen letters of 'by the actor due a' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Older television sets were built around this picture tube, so it was a component of the set; the question mark flags the dated example.

clue.text: Inclined to be hypersensitive, if there's a theme

parts.note: a theme is the subject or topic of a discussion

explanation.surface: Someone touchy whenever a particular subject comes up in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for a hereditary tendency to allergic reactions such as eczema and hay fever, i.e. a predisposition to hypersensitivity.

clue.text: Ill-defined situation roughly a year after a bit of work turned up

indicators.note: after places the shuffled year letters behind the work unit
in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an erg is a small unit of work in physics

indicators.note: roughly means the letters of 'a year' are rearranged loosely

explanation.surface: A vague state of affairs after a year in which a little work emerged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of work' is the physics unit, not a small task; 'turned up' reads it upwards, as suits a down clue, and 'roughly' shuffles 'a year', which 'after' sets behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a matter that is neither clearly one thing nor another, a situation without sharp boundaries.

clue.text: Girl after cold drink

indicators.note: after puts the girl's name behind the cold letter

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Ava is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman following up with a chilled beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish sparkling wine, so it is an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Wrongly instructs girl about credit supply

indicators.note: about means the girl's word goes round the other piece

parts.note: miss is a form of address for a girl or young woman

indicators.note: supply read as 'supplely', bending the letters of credit into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone giving bad directions to a young woman about a source of credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is the adverb of supple, bending the letters of 'credit' into DIRECT; 'about' wraps the girl round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdirect is to give wrong guidance or orders, so the verb matches instructing someone badly.

clue.text: Word from bible: antonym for "shed"

indicators.note: the answer is a word taken out of the run of letters in 'bible: antonym'

explanation.surface: Looking up the opposite of 'shed' in a scriptural concordance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'bible' into 'antonym'. 'shed' looks like the word whose antonym is wanted; it is the definition as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall, its roof resting on the larger building.

clue.text: Honeysuckles left waiting in readiness by artist

parts.note: on ice is an idiom for something held in reserve until needed
RA, a Royal Academician, is a stock crossword artist; 'by' places him alongside

explanation.surface: Climbing flowers being left ready for a painter to depict.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus name covering all the honeysuckle species, so it names the plants collectively.

clue.text: Lovers reared on Handel composition

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so these letters are composed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Two sweethearts brought up on a piece of Handel's music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks like part of the musical picture; it is the anagram signal, rearranging all fourteen letters of 'reared on Handel'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this pair were famous sweethearts: he swam the Hellespont nightly to see her and drowned.

clue.text: Electoral system briefly in favour

parts.note: the abbreviation AV for this voting method sits inside the word 'favour'

explanation.surface: A voting method that was, for a short time, popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' asks for the system's short form, AV, and those two letters are found 'in' fAVour; the surface instead suggests the system was only briefly popular. The UK rejected it in a 2011 referendum.
explanation.definitionFit: A preferential voting method in which electors rank candidates, the second preferences of eliminated candidates being redistributed.

clue.text: Bloke heading off to party, extremely drunk

indicators.note: the head, the first letter of the bloke's word, is removed

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a man

indicators.note: extremely means the outermost letters of party are taken

explanation.surface: A man setting off for a party already very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' takes C from CHAP, leaving HAP; 'extremely' gives PY, the ends of 'party'.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy is a mild colloquial term for tipsy, slightly the worse for drink.

clue.text: An older relative can ring about daughter moving rather slowly

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A

indicators.note: about means the chain of pieces goes round the next letter

parts.note: nan is a grandmother
a tin is a can
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A grandmother who can phone her daughter, though she gets about rather slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a telephone call but is the round letter; 'about' puts the daughter just after the first N of the whole chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning a little faster than andante, a moderately slow walking pace.

clue.text: One that dresses in red coat, splashed with yellow

indicators.note: splashed suggests the letters of red coat are scattered and spread anew

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A soldier's scarlet coat that has been spattered with yellow paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashed' rearranges REDCOAT to DECORAT; OR is the heraldic tincture for gold or yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator dresses a room or shop window, adorning it with paint, paper or display.

clue.text: Model has drunk a gin with lime — swallowing small pips, perhaps

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car

indicators.note: swallowing means the shuffled letters take in the next piece
drunk means the letters of a gin and lime are reeling into a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A fashion model downing a gimlet-style drink, pips and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges AGINLIME to IMEIGNAL, which 'swallowing' wraps round S; 'pips' are the Greenwich time beeps on BBC radio, not fruit seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The pips are a series of short beeps broadcast on BBC radio to mark the exact hour, an example of an audible clock marker.

clue.text: Circular letter very good as a final letter

parts.note: O is the round letter of the alphabet
mega is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A mailshot that works well as the last letter sent.
explanation.definitionFit: The last character of the Greek alphabet, so it is literally the closing letter.

clue.text: See 8
Former PM, say, entertained by sheep farmer?

indicators.note: entertained by means the word say is held between the sheep and the farmer

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
Old MacDonald, of the nursery song, had a farm

explanation.surface: A one-time prime minister, for instance, being hosted by someone who keeps sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is not an example marker but the word itself, held by the sheep and the farmer: Old MacDonald of the children's song.
explanation.definitionFit: He was Britain's first Labour prime minister, leading governments in 1924 and 1929 to 1935.

clue.text: Those ruining fisherman's afternoon?

parts.note: read as 'after noon': M, for meridian or noon, comes first and the fisherman's word follows it
an angler is a fisherman; the possessive supplies the final S

explanation.surface: Things spoiling a peaceful afternoon on the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afternoon' splits as 'after noon': the angler's word comes after M, which stands for noon (meridies, as in a.m. and p.m.).
explanation.definitionFit: To mangle something is to spoil or wreck it, so people or things that mangle are wreckers.

clue.text: Bumpkin catches elver swimming on the other side

indicators.note: catches means the lout's word goes round the other letters

parts.note: an oaf is a clumsy country lout

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of elver are moving about

explanation.surface: A country yokel netting a young eel swimming on the far bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges ELVER to VERLE, which OAF 'catches'.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed on the reverse of the page, as in the note 'see over' at the foot of a sheet.

clue.text: A long time in that state

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in 'yon hill'
KS is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kansas

explanation.surface: Something has been in a certain condition for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for ages, a very long period, as in 'I haven't seen her in donkey's years'.

clue.text: Drink during the day? On a downhill course there

definitions.note: the phrase points to the slope where such a skier would be, the noun for that course

indicators.note: during means the drink goes within the day

parts.note: Sun is the abbreviation for Sunday
kir is white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: Après-ski drinking in the sunshine, then off down the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the day' is Sunday in short, not sunshine; 'during' puts the blackcurrant drink inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A marked trail down a mountain for skiers, a downhill course on snow.

clue.text: Awfully messy site gets put in order

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of messy site are in a terrible jumble to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadfully untidy building site is finally tidied up.
explanation.definitionFit: To systemise is to arrange according to a method, organising things into proper order.

clue.text: Challenge "this setter's a dog" notion, initially

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so 'this setter is' gives I'M
a pug is a small breed of dog

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of notion

explanation.surface: Disputing the idea that the crossword compiler is a cur.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn is to call into question or dispute the truth or honesty of something.

clue.text: Lecture chess player taking time over capturing piece

indicators.note: capturing means the preceding pieces close round the next one

parts.note: Mikhail Tal was a Latvian world chess champion
O for over, from cricket scoring
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A grandmaster taking too long over winning a piece earns a reprimand.
explanation.walkthrough: Mikhail Tal was world chess champion in 1960; the surface's 'capturing piece' is a chess move, but here it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing-down or reprimand; a lecture in the scolding sense.

clue.text: See 1
Something to eat? Yes, right away!

parts.note: OK is an informal yes
A stands for away in football fixtures

explanation.surface: An eager agreement to fetch some food immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: A green pod vegetable, also called ladies' fingers, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Where sheep might be found by the French Marine?

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article
a pen is an enclosure for sheep

explanation.surface: A seaside sheepfold, perhaps near a French soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine' is not a sea soldier but the first name of the French politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine is the forename of the French far-right politician, so her surname completes the name.

clue.text: One of the British Isles needs alerting about possible danger area

parts.note: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory in the Atlantic

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of alerting are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: An island needing warnings about a hazardous stretch nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ALERTING to TRIANGLE. Bermuda is British-ruled but loosely called one of the British isles here.
explanation.definitionFit: A region of the western Atlantic of legend, where ships and aircraft are said to have vanished mysteriously.
